questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a strong desire to pursue an area of study, that I had become interested in during the previous semester. I then compared programs for the subject, security studies, between the Us partners that UCPH had. That compared with my general feeling of the different universities led me to pick CU Boulder.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I recall not having any issues.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an welcome seminar with the person responsible for exchange students at CU, and I had a correspondence with the student councilor at the department of political science and anthropology.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, there was both an off-campus housing portal managed by CU and multiple Facebook groups. I found housing through the latter.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's what most people do and it's a lot cheaper than on-campus housing. Having roomies is also a good way to have a network.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course catalogue was easy to navigate and then you just picked the classes you wanted, and if there was free spaces and you fulfilled the requirements you were accepted. If not you were placed on a waitlist. I was on multiple waitlists but ended up getting all my first choices.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Plenty, mainly study councilors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all my first choices.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one intro level course and three senior levels.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More course work(quiz, test, discussion posts, etc.) and less critical independent work. More focus on a recital and less on engaging critically with the material you read.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PACS 2500 Introduction to Peace, Conflict and Security
PACS 3800 Security Studies
PSCI 4012 Global Development
ANTH 4180 Anthropology of Refugees and War

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed PACS 3800 a lot, mainly due to the professor. Also ANTH 4180 was a very different approach to studying with a large emphasis on independent work and alternative teaching which was interesting. Again highly dependent on the professor.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A car broke down.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive, in general it was very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't really participate in any, but there was a large student recreations center which was free to use. Also a pool.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Student Rec Center, multiple festivals during the semester, international film club, a lot of student organizations.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the pool when it stops snowing and springs arrives.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a trip to Utah during a weekend, it's a 6 hour drive and amazing. Go to Moab specifically.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not that difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get roommates.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are younger at college than most people are at uni, and they felt somewhat immature in general.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Chipotle was great, people were also very nice and sociable.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Expect rent and living to be very expensive.
Prepare for a lot of busy work and that is easy but takes a while to complete.
Remember your grades don't matter, you just need to pass so have a good time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's a surprisingly small campus and there's a lot of engineering and business majors compared to arts and sciences.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Building friendships with my roomies and feeling that I learned the academics I set out to understand.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Affording rent and food.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
